proof:
# Log-concave integer tails at an integer mean

Let p_k be a probability sequence of finite interval support
{l,l+1,...,r}, positive on this support, and assume

    p_k^2>=p_(k-1)p_(k+1).

If its mean m=sum k p_k is an integer, then

    sum_(k>=m) p_k>=1/e,       sum_(k<=m)p_k>=1/e.       (1)

This is a direct finite discrete Jensen argument.

Define F(k)=sum_(j>=k)p_j. The ratios p_(k+1)/p_k are nonincreasing.
For each fixed j>=0 the ratio p_(k+j)/p_k, interpreted as zero beyond the
right endpoint, is therefore nonincreasing in k: it is a product of j
successive nonincreasing positive ratios until that endpoint. Hence

    F(k)/p_k=sum_(j>=0)p_(k+j)/p_k

is nonincreasing. Thus p_k/F(k) is nondecreasing, and

    F(k+1)/F(k)=1-p_k/F(k)

is nonincreasing for l<=k<r. The sequence F is log-concave where it is
positive. Its log has a concave piecewise-linear interpolation on [l,r].
Jensen at the integer mean consequently gives

    log F(m)>=sum_k p_k log F(k).

Use F(r+1)=0 and p_k=F(k)-F(k+1). Since log t is increasing,

    p_k log F(k)>=integral_(F(k+1))^(F(k)) log t dt.

The improper integral at the last interval's lower endpoint 0 is finite.
Summing over the partition of [0,1] gives

    sum_k p_k log F(k)>=integral_0^1 log t dt=-1.

This proves the first inequality in (1); reflecting the sequence proves
the second. If the support is a singleton, both tails are one directly.
For a nontrivial positive interval support the mean is strictly between
the two endpoints, so no undefined log at r+1 is ever evaluated by Jensen.
All probabilities at the tested integer m are included, as required for
closed halfspaces.

## Consequence for vertical caps at a mixed centroid when n=1

Let C subset R x R^d be a convex body, d>=1, with positive mixed d-volume
M. The positive-volume integer fiber indices form an interval: ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski makes the dth root of continuous fiber volume concave on
its positive domain. In particular its positive integer samples a_k are
log-concave. One may see the latter directly from

    a_k^(1/d)>=[a_(k-1)^(1/d)+a_(k+1)^(1/d)]/2
               >=(a_(k-1)a_(k+1))^(1/(2d)).

Zero-volume endpoint fibers can be removed from the probability support;
they have no effect on its mean or tails. Normalize p_k=a_k/M. If the
actual mixed-volume centroid has integer base m, then every closed
vertical ambient halfspace containing that centroid contains either
{k>=m} or {k<=m}. Its mass is therefore at least M/e.

This exceeds gamma_d M/2 for every d>=1. Indeed gamma_d<=1/2 follows
from (1+1/d)^d>=2 by the binomial theorem, while e<3 implies 1/e>1/3>1/4.
For example e<3 follows from j!>=2^(j-1) for j>=2, strictly for j>=3,
by summing the exponential series.

This treats the vertical-cap part of the n=1 conditional-centroid problem.
It does not establish a relation for oblique caps or for sums of oblique
fiber tail profiles. In the separate d=0 case, n=1 gives a consecutive
integer interval with uniform counting measure; an integer mean is its
midpoint, and both closed tails have at least half the points directly.
